descriptionChirho: An Aramaic noun (אֱנָשׁ) meaning 'man' or 'mankind', cognate to Hebrew אֱנוֹשׁ. This word appears exclusively in the Aramaic portions of Daniel and Ezra. In the singular absolute form (אֱנָשׁ), it denotes an individual human being or 'man' generically, as in Daniel's visions where one 'like a son of man' (כְּבַר אֱנָשׁ, Dan 7:13) appears, and in the narrative of Dan 2:10, 3:10, 5:5, 7, 6:7, 12, and Ezra 4:11, 6:11. In the emphatic/determined plural form (אֲנָשָׁא), it denotes 'men/mankind' collectively, especially in Nebuchadnezzar's declarations about God's sovereignty over human kingdoms (Dan 2:38, 43; 4:16-17, 25, 32-33; 5:21). The Ketiv/Qere variants (אנושא/אֲנָשָׁא in Dan 4:16-17) are orthographic alternatives of the same word, not distinct senses. The construct form 'men of' (Ezra 4:11) is a syntactic variant. All clusters represent a single Aramaic lexeme meaning 'man/mankind' in various morphological forms.
